# Core Commands

Every command the `core` module offers, from its declarations, in order of the resource each acts on. Each command's help says the same.

## Aliases

A group's alias is a word a person may type in place of its own, declared in the module's `[aliases]`. `lnk module` is typed short as `lnk mod`.

## Core

### `lnk help`

Show Link's commands or the help for one command

```usage
lnk help [group] [-- <arguments>...] [--json]
```

- `arguments`, after `--`, list of string: The command within the group
- `group`, position 1, string: The command group whose help to read
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk uninstall`

Uninstall `lnk` and its modules, stopping what they run.

```usage
lnk uninstall [--all] [--delete <delete>] [--json] [--yes]
```

- `--all`, boolean: Also delete every part
- `--delete`, list of string: Also delete a named part (repeat, or comma-separated)
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It answers `core.kept`.

### `lnk up`

Set up `lnk`: choose what you want it for, and it installs the modules that needs

```usage
lnk up [uses] [--json] [--module <module>] [--source <source>] [--stale]
```

- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `--module`, list of string: Select source modules by executable name without lnk-; separate names with commas or repeat the flag
- `--source`, list of path: Install supported modules from a source workspace with Cargo
- `--stale`, boolean: Refresh only installed source modules whose Cargo build differs from the installed executable
- `uses`, position 1, list of string: What you want Link for (`agents`) [default: asks]

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk upgrade`

Upgrade `lnk` and its modules to the latest release (or a specific version)

```usage
lnk upgrade [version] [--check] [--json] [--yes]
```

- `--check`, boolean: Report newer releases and advisories, installing nothing. Ordinary interactive commands refresh this guidance in the background
- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `version`, position 1, string: Version to install, e.g. 0.14.0 [default: the latest release]
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It answers `core.report`.

## Folder

### `lnk folder check`

List old atomic-write staging files in your data without deleting them

```usage
lnk folder check [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `core.staging`.

### `lnk folder create`

Make a new, empty Link folder at `~/Link`, in place of one that's gone

```usage
lnk folder create [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `core.folder`.

### `lnk folder list`

List the map: each location, by its ID, and where it is on this machine, starting with the Link folder

```usage
lnk folder list [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `core.map`.

### `lnk folder set`

Move a location to a path: its files, when they're there, and its entry in the map, with every location inside it; or point Link at files you moved

```usage
lnk folder set <location> <path> [--json]
```

- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `location`, position 1, string, required: The location's ID, as `lnk folder list` shows it: link for the Link folder
- `path`, position 2, path, required: Where it goes, or where you moved it

It answers `core.folder`.

## Issue

### `lnk issue create`

Turn the last failure into a bug report: its fields, scrubbed of what's private, to paste, or filled in on the bug form with --open

```usage
lnk issue create [--json] [--open]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `--open`, boolean: Open the bug form in your browser with what fits filled in. It answers `core.report`.

## Module

### `lnk module add`

Add modules: Link's by name, or one from outside Link by --url

```usage
lnk module add [modules] [--json] [--signer <signer>] [--url <url>] [--yes]
```

- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `modules`, position 1, list of string: Link's modules by name (`lnk module list`)
- `--signer`, string: Trust this signer (ssh-ed25519 ...) rather than the one its release offers
- `--url`, list of string: A module from outside Link, by its GitHub URL, https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> (repeat)
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk module list`

List Link's modules, which are installed, and those from outside Link (the default)

```usage
lnk module list [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers list of `core.module`.

### `lnk module remove`

Remove modules, and what needs them

```usage
lnk module remove <modules> [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `modules`, position 1, list of string, required: The modules, as `lnk module list` names them. It answers `core.report`.

### `lnk module show`

Show where a module comes from and whether it's installed

```usage
lnk module show <module> [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `module`, position 1, string, required: The module, as `lnk module list` names it. It answers `core.module`.

## Variable

### `lnk variable list`

List command environment variable names and descriptions, optionally for one command, without reading their values

```usage
lnk variable list [command] [--json]
```

It takes `command`, position 1, list of string: Command words to inspect, such as agent start; omit to list all command declarations. It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers list of `core.variable`.
